minutes.headline: Joint meeting with School Committee reached informal consensus to advance phases one and two; Turkey Hill and phase three left open.
minutes.summary: The Municipal Building Design Committee met jointly with the School Committee to discuss how the phased plan (Ritter renovation and new town hall annex, then Town Hall as a meeting house, then TC Pasos/Turkey Hill) overlaps with the future of Turkey Hill Elementary. The debate was heated over Turkey Hill's condition, MSBA 10-year school-use rules, debt capacity and maintenance. No formal vote was taken on the plan; the chair found informal consensus, and both bodies adjourned.

budget_items.what_was_said: The Turkey Hill work sits in the capital plan around a placeholder year only because it needs to be somewhere; no date is firm.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill renovation vs. new school
budget_items.what_was_said: Chair argued a renovation investment while school-owned could draw reimbursement that is lost once the building leaves school hands.
A school member said debt capacity likely cannot support phases one and two plus a new school, with interest rates having risen.

budget_items.topic: Architectural and engineering funds for the municipal plan
budget_items.what_was_said: The committee has funds set up for architectural/engineering costs to learn actual cost of the work.
Chair framed whether taking state money and committing to 10 years of school use is worth it versus adding the cost to a future disposition.
Town manager said town-side vacancies amount to a large number of hours per week and cited building conditions.
Superintendent said the submitted capital plan already includes an engineering study of Turkey Hill.
A member cited the new primary school's cost and ongoing work, with MSBA covering about half.

decisions.decision: No formal vote on the plan; the chair declared informal consensus to keep working together, with homework on both sides before the next meeting.
Chair sought consensus that the committee advance phases one and two and continue developing phase three, including Turkey Hill and TC Pasos disposition; school members indicated general agreement.
ARPA funding commitment, RFP language and special town meeting community update article deferred to the next meeting.
Next meeting set for Monday, November 6th; meetings are first and third Mondays at 6 PM via Zoom.
School chair agreed to have the new facilities manager engage with the Green Communities committee.

what_happened.line: No formal vote was taken; the chair declared informal consensus to keep working together, with homework for both bodies before the next meeting.
The chair sought consensus to advance phases one and two and keep developing phase three, including Turkey Hill and TC Pasos; school members indicated general agreement.
School-side members said Turkey Hill needs capital work on its roof, windows, HVAC, electrical, plumbing and ADA access, with or without state funding.
A school member said debt capacity likely cannot support phases one and two plus a new school, with interest rates having risen.
The ARPA funding commitment, RFP language and a special town meeting update article were deferred to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: Whether Turkey Hill is renovated, replaced or sold, and how a town hall project is paid for, shapes future debt and so future tax bills, but nothing was voted and no cost or date is fixed.
Taking state school-building money would commit the building to 10 years of school use, so that choice affects what the town can do with the site and its other buildings.
watch_next: Next meeting Monday, November 6th at 6 PM via Zoom, where the ARPA commitment, RFP language and town meeting article are due.
Any written plan or cost for phase three, covering Turkey Hill and TC Pasos, and the engineering study the superintendent said is in the submitted capital plan.
